versions.name: RXV2-0.9.725-fewer-words
versions.notes: Far fewer words on screen (Malcolm: 'too many words - the explanations can be in the help screens, this is true across the whole app'). Nothing is lost: every explanation moved into that page's ? help, in full. About 1000 words came off the pages this pass - the update page (install-over choice, progress line, failure message, and release notes now clipped to two lines, tap for the rest), Receiver settings, WiFi, Dongle, the welcome and bind panels on the front page, and Travel extents. Safety and consequence lines stay, cut to one sentence. The step-by-step guides keep their words, because there the instructions are the point.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.724-teal-check
versions.notes: The Check for a Rotorflight update button was grey, which reads as disabled (Malcolm spotted it). It is now teal with an icon, like the buttons above it. The demo now answers the check properly too - its flight controller is a real 4.6.0, so it says 'up to date' as a real receiver would, instead of 'could not check' on a phone that plainly has internet.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.723-check-now
versions.notes: Check for a Rotorflight update, when YOU ask (Malcolm's suggestion). A button at the foot of the Rotorflight page asks, there and then, whether a newer Rotorflight has come out - so nothing runs on a timer and nothing waits to surprise you. It gives one of three plain answers: up to date; a newer one is available (with 'back up first - flashing erases everything', and the reminder that flashing itself needs the Configurator on a computer); or a newer one is out but these pages have not been checked against it yet, so stay where you are. It asks two places: our own checked recommendation, and Rotorflight's own releases live - so it cannot answer 'up to date' for weeks after a real release. It never recommends a release our tuning pages have not been checked against, and when it cannot reach the internet it says so instead of guessing. Two preview buttons in the page's help show the other two answers without waiting months for a release. Needs internet on the phone or the receiver; the daily automatic check is gone.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.722-better-chance
versions.notes: Better wording on the Firmware page: Bluetooth is slower but stands a better chance of success in these circumstances. Includes 0.9.721.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.721-lane-buttons
versions.notes: The Firmware page now has two plain buttons - Receiver WiFi and Bluetooth - so you can see and choose how an update travels, instead of a note that only appeared sometimes. The one in use is ticked, and a line underneath says why you might want the other. If the receiver has no WiFi of its own, Bluetooth is chosen for you. Includes 0.9.720.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.720-patient-install
versions.notes: An install that was simply taking a long time was being reported as a failure. The page gave it two and a half minutes, which is plenty on a good signal and not nearly enough on a weak one. It now says 'still going' and keeps watching for another three minutes before it says anything went wrong - and if it cannot actually see the new version with its own eyes, it says so rather than claiming success. Includes 0.9.719.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.719-weak-wifi-choice
versions.notes: When the receiver's WiFi is weak, the Firmware page now says so before you start and offers Bluetooth instead - slower, but it does not depend on the weak signal. And if a WiFi install does crawl and fail, there is now a button to try again over Bluetooth rather than leaving you to work it out. The old firmware is untouched either way. Includes 0.9.718.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.718-rf-check-daily
versions.notes: The Rotorflight update check now happens once a day, on the first time you open the app that day, and never makes you wait for it - anything it already knows is shown at once and the check happens quietly behind. If it cannot reach the internet it tries again in an hour rather than giving up for the day. Includes 0.9.717.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.717-rf-update-hint
versions.notes: The Rotorflight page can now tell you when a newer Rotorflight has come out - the one job these pages cannot do for you. It says nothing at all unless there is something worth acting on, it tells you to back up first because flashing erases everything, and if the new release is one these pages have not been checked against yet it says the opposite: stay where you are, there is no hurry. Includes 0.9.716.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.716-dongle-power
versions.notes: The dongle's Wiring section now warns that if you also run a USB cable to the flight controller, the dongle's 5 V must come from the flight controller itself and not from a separate supply - the dongle puts 5 V down that cable, so a second supply would meet the flight controller's own 5 V through it. It also explains that D5 and D6 become a fallback once USB is in use. Includes 0.9.715.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.715-safety-gates
versions.notes: Safety review fixes. Capturing or clearing the failsafe positions is now refused while the model is armed - capturing on an armed model would have stored the arming switch ON as the failsafe position. Installing firmware is refused while the transmitter is on, because the receiver stops sending control frames for the whole download. Bringing the radios back after a flight now parks the output safely instead of restarting bare. And a dongle no longer writes control frames into the flight controller's settings port while waiting for a reply. Includes 0.9.714.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.714-adaptive-poll
versions.notes: View channels now adapts. It asks briskly until the receiver's fast push actually starts working, and only then stands back to let the push do the work. Before, it always stood back - which was slower than it used to be whenever the push did not start. It can no longer be slower than it was. Includes 0.9.713.

rotorflight.line: Rotorflight 2.3 — the release these pages are written and tested against.
